concerns.text: Phase 6 (T036–T044) introduces features (Blind Agent, Forgetting/Decay, Noise & Coherence, Adaptive Noise, Consolidation, extended Scaling) that are absent from spec.md and plan.md. This constitutes scope creep and violates the Constitution's 'Single Source of Truth' (Principle IV) and 'Reproducibility' (Principle I) by implementing unverified requirements not sanctioned by the spec.

Tasks T036–T044 include non-technical metadata ('Reviewer: Alan Turing', etc.) in task descriptions. This violates the Constitution's 'Data Hygiene' (Principle III) and 'Reproducibility' (Principle I) by introducing non-deterministic, non-technical attribution into the implementation plan, risking template placeholder rejection.

FR-008 mandates a sensitivity analysis sweeping token limits over the specific set {128, 256, 512}. Task T022 describes sweeping 'a range of representative values (e.g., low, medium, and high)' without enforcing the exact numeric thresholds. This is a semantic weakening of the functional requirement.

Plan.md Methodology explicitly rejects 'Separate One-Way ANOVAs' in favor of a 'Mixed-Design ANOVA' to correctly model the Context × Metric interaction. Task T020 instructs implementing a 'single two-way independent-samples ANOVA', which is a statistical category error (treating Metric as a between-subjects factor) and contradicts the approved plan's methodological correction.

Spec.md US-1 and FR-001 require 1,000 games for the baseline. Plan.md 'Compute Feasibility' explicitly targets N=200 for CPU runs and defers N=1000 to GPU. Task T015 mandates 1000 games without conditioning this on the execution environment, creating a conflict that risks task failure on the constrained CPU runner defined in the plan.

SC-005 requires the scaling plot to include a note that '3 data points limit power-law reliability'. Task T030 requires the note to be present but does not specify the exact phrasing or ensure legibility/extractability, risking a verification failure if the note is omitted or obscured in the PDF output.
